focus: Auto/confirm YAML twins as pairs: deep-review and deep-ai-council differential, then the review YAML's synthesis and verdict steps against deep-review/references

graphEvents.label: Does the review auto twin's synthesis and verdict path implement what deep-review/references specifies?
releaseReadinessState is initialized in-progress and never transitioned by either twin
ai-council confirm twin carries no post_dispatch_validate, route proof or progress_liveness
Two contradictory resolved_route spellings in one council step with route_proof_mismatch as a failure reason
step_generate_state_summary emits a documentation pipe-enum as a placeholder, auto-only
Two restart implementations; the live auto one skips generation and parent_session_id bookkeeping

label: DRIFT (both twins): releaseReadinessState is written exactly once per run as "in-progress" and no step ever transitions it, so a converged review reports in-progress forever. A whole-file grep for the field name in deep-review-auto.yaml and deep-review-confirm.yaml returns only the initializer (auto:541, confirm:522); step_update_config_status sets only status:"complete" (auto:2508, confirm:1963). The reference contract declares a three-value enum in-progress/converged/release-blocking and requires the final report to record which one applies (state/state-format.md:150, protocol/completion-criteria.md:74), and calls the field "the canonical config/report field for review readiness tracking" (protocol/quick-reference.md:132). Because nothing assigns converged or release-blocking, the enum's other two members are declared but unreachable, and the released review packet's own config contradicts its report verdict.

DRIFT (twin asymmetry, council): deep-ai-council-auto.yaml carries a post_dispatch_validate block with validator session-state-hierarchy.cjs#validateSessionStateHierarchy, an assert_jsonl_record_type round_completed assertion, an assert_jsonl_fields list and a route_proof (auto:175-186), plus a progress_liveness contract block (auto:168). deep-ai-council-confirm.yaml contains none of these: a grep for post_dispatch_validate, resolved_route, progress_liveness and step_map_topic_state over the confirm twin returns zero hits. The confirm twin is the mode an operator is watching interactively and the mode whose artifacts are most likely to be hand-inspected, yet it is the only one of the pair that never asserts the round_completed record shape, never proves the AI Council route was loaded, and has no per-seat persistence contract, so a confirm-mode session can complete with a session-state file that the auto mode would have rejected as route_proof_missing.

DRIFT (self-contradicting route string): within a single step of deep-ai-council-auto.yaml the same resolved route is spelled two different ways. The step's own output list declares resolved_route_header as "Resolved route: mode=ai-council; target_agent=@ai-council; execution=multi_topic_session_round; state_source=ai-council/session-state.jsonl; depth_aware=true; do_not_switch_mode=true" (auto:159) with semicolon separators and an @-prefixed agent, while the post_dispatch_validate route_proof in the same step declares resolved_route as "Resolved route: mode=ai-council target_agent=ai-council" (auto:183) with space separators, no @, and four of the six fields dropped. step route_proof lists route_proof_mismatch among its failure_reasons (auto:184), so an exact-comparison validator fails the run against whichever of the two spellings it disagrees with; a normalising validator silently accepts two different route identities. Either way the reference header is not a single value.

DRIFT (doc notation compiled into runtime): deep-review-auto.yaml's step_generate_state_summary emits the line "Provisional Verdict: {PASS|CONDITIONAL|FAIL|PENDING} hasAdvisories={has_advisories}" (auto:1148ff) into the per-iteration dispatch prompt. That literal, pipe-separated brace group is documentation notation copied verbatim from the protocol reference, which writes the same pattern as a template in a fenced spec example (protocol/loop-protocol.md:243, and the same shape at loop-protocol.md:403). No step binds a token named PASS|CONDITIONAL|FAIL|PENDING, and verdict is only derived later in step_derive_verdict inside phase_synthesis (auto:2333), so during the loop the dispatch prompt carries either the raw pipe-enum or an unresolved token on every iteration. The step is auto-only: deep-review-confirm.yaml has no step_generate_state_summary at all, so the confirm twin avoids the defect by having no state summary.

DRIFT (two restart implementations, the live one loses lineage bookkeeping): deep-review-auto.yaml adds step_apply_lifecycle_request (auto:186ff) ahead of fan-out and normal init, whose only declared outputs are archived_path and lineage_mode:"restart" — it archives the packet under the review-archive root and recreates the directory but sets neither parent_session_id nor generation. step_classify_session's on_restart branch (auto, in the step beginning at 338) sets parent_session_id and generation "{prior_generation + 1}", but step_apply_lifecycle_request has already emptied the packet directory, so classify_session resolves the session as fresh and on_restart cannot fire on that path; the note's lifecycle_routing rule can therefore only fire for a restart that did not come through the lifecycle request. The reference contract requires the config's lineage block to match the current run, naming parentSessionId, lineageMode, generation and continuedFromRun explicitly (protocol/completion-criteria.md:57, protocol/loop-protocol.md:123), so an auto restart produces a config whose generation is inherited unchanged and whose parentSessionId is absent — a new segment that claims continuity it does not record. Confirm mode has no step_apply_lifecycle_request and its on_resume restart option sets both fields, so the defect is introduced by the auto twin.

direction: Auto-resume loses the iteration and severity counters that confirm mode restores at gate_init_approval (confirm on_A sets current_iteration, stuck_count, p0_count, p1_count, p2_count; auto on_resume jumps straight to phase_loop).
reason: Falsified by reading step_read_state in both twins: its extract list derives current_iteration as iteration_count+1 and recomputes p0_count, p1_count and p2_count by scanning all iteration records, so the counters are restored from state rather than from the gate. The apparent gap is a non-issue and the auto path is if anything more accurate on resume.

direction: Removing the approval gates from the auto review twin is itself a defect worth reporting.
reason: Not a defect: the twin declares workflow_execution: autonomous and approvals: none at its head, the removed gates are the same operations re-expressed as log/set/proceed_to steps, and the recovered branching (gate_pre_iteration on_B adjust focus, gate_post_iteration, gate_pre_synthesis on_B run more iterations) has no meaning without an operator to answer it. Only the asymmetries listed as findings survive that reading.
